findings.title: Negative-offset queryset slicing raises an exception, so the 'advanced pagination' path always fails
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code executes `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices: it raises `AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported") unless a negative step is used, and with a step it's not valid SQL OFFSET semantics. The comment claiming 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false. Any client that sends a cursor with a negative offset while using optimized_pagination=true will get a 500 error; the feature can never return data.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward-cursor offsets to 0 instead of rejecting them
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` alters behavior for all existing paginators (Paginator, DateTimePaginator, etc.). Previously, a malformed/corrupted cursor with a negative offset on a forward page would surface as an error from queryset slicing; now it is silently clamped to 0 and the client receives the first page of results while believing it is on a later page. This masks cursor corruption and can produce silently wrong data (e.g., duplicate rows already seen). For is_prev cursors the negative offset is still passed through, so it will raise an exception from the ORM — inconsistent behavior between the two directions. The correct fix is to validate and reject negative offsets (as OffsetPaginator and ChainPaginator do with BadPaginationError).

findings.title: New undocumented 'optimized_pagination' query parameter and superuser-gated paginator add no functionality and can 500
findings.body: The endpoint adds an undocumented, EXPERIMENTAL-status query parameter `optimized_pagination` that switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True for superusers/global-access users. Since the advanced path only activates for negative cursor offsets and that path always raises an exception when slicing the queryset, this flag is a purely additive way for privileged clients to trigger server errors. There is no test coverage for the new parameter or the new paginator, and no documentation of the parameter's contract. Additionally, the gating on is_superuser/has_global_access suggests a security boundary, but the comment in the paginator ('safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') reveals the queryset is already org-scoped — the permission gate provides no actual protection and is misleading.

findings.title: is_prev length check uses raw (possibly negative) offset, so the trailing-row trim never fires for advanced cursors
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when a previous-page cursor with a value is used together with a negative offset (the advanced path), the check `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares against the original (negative) offset, while the results were fetched using `start_offset = cursor.offset` and `stop = start_offset + limit + extra`. The length of the fetched slice can never equal a negative-plus-limit sum in the intended way, so the extra boundary row is never trimmed, resulting in off-by-one duplicate/missing rows at page boundaries for previous-page navigation.

findings.title: Comment in Cursor implies negative offsets are a supported general feature
findings.body: The added comment on Cursor.offset states that negative offsets are allowed for 'advanced pagination scenarios', but nothing in Cursor.from_string or anywhere else validates or supports them coherently: other paginators (SequencePaginator, OffsetPaginator, ChainPaginator) explicitly assert or raise on negative offsets, while BasePaginator-based ones now either clamp them silently or crash depending on is_prev. The comment documents behavior that does not exist and will mislead maintainers.
